findings.title: isAccessTokenId never actually checks the grant shortcut
findings.body: The grant shortcut sits at index 4–5 of the 6-character prefix, but the code reads `substring(3, 5)`. For `onrtac` that gives `ta`. The condition is also inverted: it returns false when the value *matches* the expected shortcut. Because the offset is wrong, the comparison never matches, so the matcher accepts any `xxxxxx:<uuid>` token ID no matter the grant type. The tests that use it (code-to-token, refresh, device, CIBA) can't catch a wrong or missing grant type. Fix: `if (items[0].length() != 6 || !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant type factories at startup
findings.body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` is a provider interface that extensions implement. Adding an abstract method means any custom factory compiled against the old interface throws `AbstractMethodError` when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `gtf.getShortcut()`. A custom factory that returns null makes `ConcurrentHashMap.put` throw an NPE. Either failure stops the server from starting. Two shortcuts that happen to collide also abort startup through the size check. Consider a `default` implementation (for example, derived from the id), and skip or fall back to `na` for null shortcuts instead of failing startup.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId tests grantType instead
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks `grantType` a second time, so a null `rawTokenId` is accepted. Encoding then produces an ID ending in `:null`. Change it to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

held.title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed
held.body: The change deletes the public `Context(Context context)` constructor, and the request doesn't call for removing it. Any grant type or extension that builds a derived context with `new Context(context)` will no longer compile. I can't see if any caller remains in the rest of the code. Also, the new constructor calls `formParams.getFirst(...)`, which throws an NPE for any caller that passes null formParams. Keep the copy constructor (and copy `grantType` in it), and null-guard `formParams`.

held.title: Every access token now needs session context client and a known grant shortcut
held.body: `initToken` now always calls `getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)`, which dereferences `session.getContext().getClient()`. Before, this only ran inside protocol mappers. Any token-creation path where the session context has no client set now fails with an NPE. Also, `encodeTokenId` throws `IllegalStateException` when a grant type set in the client session context has no registered factory or shortcut, so token issuance fails instead of falling back to `na`. Fall back to the client argument and to UNKNOWN rather than failing.
